title: Check yourself: Function and its relatives

questions.stem: A config loader holds `Function<String, String> expand = v -> v.replace("${APP}", "/srv/app");` and a mutable `List<String> paths`. A teammate adds `paths.replaceAll(expand);`. What happens?

options.text: It compiles and expands every path, since a Function<String, String> counts as a UnaryOperator<String> wherever one is asked for
options.says: UnaryOperator<T> extends Function<T, T>, not the other way round; a Function value doesn't count as a UnaryOperator

options.text: It compiles and expands every path, since the compiler adapts any variable whose lambda has the shape replaceAll calls
options.says: only a lambda or method reference written in the call takes the type the call asks for; a variable keeps the type it was declared with

options.text: It does not compile, since a Function<String, String> doesn't count as a UnaryOperator<String> wherever one is asked for
options.says: UnaryOperator<T> extends Function<T, T>, not the other way round; a lambda written in the call would compile, a Function variable doesn't

options.text: It does not compile, since the compiler adapts no variable to the type replaceAll calls, whatever the variable's declared type
options.says: a variable declared as UnaryOperator<String> is accepted; the refusal is about the declared type, not about passing a variable

origin.section: UnaryOperator<T> Is a Function<T, T>, but a Function<T, T> Is Not a UnaryOperator<T>

questions.stem: An HR export builds `staff.stream().collect(Collectors.toMap(Employee::id, Employee::managerId, (a, b) -> a))`. Every id is distinct. One contractor's managerId is null. What does the export get?

options.text: A map without the contractor, since the collector drops an element whose value mapper returns null before it reaches the map
options.says: nothing is skipped; the null reaches Map.merge and is rejected

options.text: A map with the contractor mapped to null, since with a merge function the collector stores values through Map.merge, which accepts null
options.says: the merge function only decides between two values for one key; it doesn't make null acceptable

options.text: A NullPointerException, since with a merge function the collector stores values through Map.merge, which rejects null
options.says: the three-argument toMap collects through Map.merge, and the run on the page shows the NullPointerException

options.text: An IllegalStateException, since the collector treats a null value as a clash the merge function is asked to settle and cannot
options.says: IllegalStateException is the duplicate-key failure of the two-argument form; with distinct ids there is no clash

origin.section: Collectors.toMap Throws on a Duplicate Key or a null Value Until You Say What to Do

questions.stem: A rate limiter keeps `Map<String, Integer> tokens`, one entry per client. Each request runs `tokens.computeIfPresent(client, (c, t) -> t > 0 ? t - 1 : null)` and is allowed when that call returns a non-null value. Every minute a job runs `tokens.replaceAll((c, t) -> 10)`. A client with 1 token left sends two requests, then waits for the next minute. What follows?

options.text: The client has 10 tokens after the job, since the null from the second request left the client's entry at 0 for replaceAll to reset
options.says: returning null from a remapping function removes the entry; it doesn't mean 'no change'

options.text: The client has 10 tokens after the job, since the null from the second request was stored in the client's entry and replaceAll reset it
options.says: the map doesn't store the null; the entry is removed, so replaceAll has nothing to overwrite

options.text: The client is refused from then on, since the null from the second request removed the client's entry and replaceAll has nothing to reset
options.says: the null removed the client, every later computeIfPresent returns null, and the refill never sees the client again

options.text: The client is refused from then on, since the null from the second request left the client's entry at 0 and replaceAll skips entries at 0
options.says: the count doesn't stay at 0: the null removed the client's entry

origin.section: A Remapping Function That Returns null Removes the Entry

questions.stem: A route planner caches `hops(station)` in a new ConcurrentHashMap with `cache.computeIfAbsent(station, s -> s.isTerminus() ? 0 : 1 + hops(s.next()))`. The line has no loops. Its unit test uses a line of 6 stations and passes. In production, on a line of 300 stations, the first query throws an IllegalStateException. What explains the difference?

options.text: With six stations the map never objected, since it notices a write from inside a computation only in some cases, such as when its table grows
options.says: the page: the map throws only when it notices; fib(13) passed and fib(14) threw when the table grew while a computation held its slot

options.text: With six stations the map never objected, since it notices a write from inside a computation only in some cases, such as when other threads write
options.says: the page's failure is single-threaded: one thread's computation inserted other keys into the same map

options.text: With six stations no limit was reached, since computeIfAbsent refuses a write from inside a computation once the map holds a fixed number of entries
options.says: there is no designed cap on entries; the exception came from a resize finding a computation still holding its slot, a write the javadoc forbids

options.text: With six stations no limit was reached, since computeIfAbsent refuses a write from inside a computation once calls nest past a fixed depth
options.says: there is no depth limit; fib(14) failed because the table grew while a computation held its slot

origin.section: A Memoized Function Must Be Pure, and Its Computation Must Not Go Back Into the Map
